newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks fall as trade data rattles market.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks fall as trade data rattles market.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended lower Wednesday as news that imports surged while foreign sales of American-made goods fell in July raised questions about the strength of the economy and whether the Federal Reserve will need to raise interest rates.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 11.47 points at 5,877.36. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,346 to 951 on moderate volume of 395 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, rose 2.40 to 1,205.71, nearing its June 5 record close of 1,249.15.

The big news was a Commerce Department report that the trade deficit ballooned by 42.6 percent in July to $11.68 billion from $8.19 billion in June. The magnitude of the deficit shocked economists, who had generally forecast a gap of $8.8 billion.

Analysts said the deficit, which is the largest since late 1987, threw into question just how robust a rate of growth the economy continues to enjoy and further muddied the near-term outlook for interest rates.

"If you're an economist, you worry a lot about this number because it says gross domestic product may be weaker than economists are forecasting for the third quarter," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
"Net exports are one of the crucial components of GDP and this says net exports are a big minus," he said.
Analysts said the weakness in U.S. exports was expected to prompt economists to lower their estimates of third-quarter economic growth.
The trade report was one of the final pieces of broad-based economic evidence before next Tuesday's meeting of the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee to review interest-rate strategy.
The Dow index soared nearly 230 points last week through Monday, setting a record high of 5,889.20 on investors' hopes that the Fed would not raise short-term interest rates.
But on Tuesday, a Reuter report that suggested some Fed members were leaning toward a hike in the discount rate revived Wall Street's jitters that the cost of borrowing may be going up.

"You have to take your hat off for the market," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist of Fahnestock & Co. He said the lack of heavy profit-taking "implies the market is not ready to correct despite nervousness, the recent sharp run up and next Tuesday's FOMC meeting."
The technology stocks were boosted by Merrill Lynch's naming of International Business Machines Corp. to its 'Focus One' stock of the week. IBM closed up 1 at 124-1/2.

"I believe my IBM earnings estimates are above consensus for the fourth quarter and if achieved, Wall Street will have greater confidence in 1997," said Daniel Mandresh, Merrill Lynch's computer industry analyst.
Other high technology shares were also big winners, with Intel Corp. up 1-3/8 to 95-5/8 and Microsoft gaining 2-5/8 to 136-1/2.

Peter Green, a technical analyst at Gruntal & Co., said the broader market has been supported by the technology group's reassertion of leadership. "It's also been helped by hopes interest rates will be left alone."
Among individual stocks, International Network Services, which provides services for complex enterprise networks, soared 92 percent or 14-3/4 points to 30-3/4 in its Wall Street debut.

Olsten lost 3-3/4 to 22-7/8 one day after the stock of ManPower, the world's largest private employment agency, tumbled on a warning that analysts' 1996 earnings estimates for the company were too high.
Tambrands rose 1-1/8 to 42-7/8 after it announced a restructuring.
Netscape lost 3-3/8 to 42-5/8. Merrill Lynch downgraded the stock, saying the company's recent new products are "sound first steps, but much more is needed to compete in the long run."
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 1.47 points to 681.47. The American Stock Exchange index was off 0.51 to 566.65.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks was off 0.99 to 363.44. The average share was down 10 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,687.157 down 14.708 or 0.22 percent.
